gap: No result ChatGPT got states that in Hi-Fi News' lab (PM, 25 Oct 2024) the Marantz MODEL M1 delivered 113 W into both 8 Ω and 4 Ω, and its dynamic power fell to 82 W into 2 Ω and 35 W into 1 Ω. In the same lab the NAD C 3050 LE gave 120 W/200 W continuous (8/4 Ω) and 275 W/252 W dynamic (4/2 Ω), the Marantz MODEL 60n beat its 60 W rating at 81 W/128 W, and Audio's lab measured the Audiolab 7000A at 76 W/127 W.
standout_why: I read Marantz's US MODEL M1 page. It gives only the maker's 100 W/125 W at 0.05% THD rating, plus EISA and Red Dot awards and one customer quote, with no independent lab data. ChatGPT's other cited results are maker pages and the Marantz infosheet PDFs, which carry maker specs only. The Audiolab and NAD product pages returned HTTP 429 when I tried them, so I could not check them line by line. They are maker or retailer pages, though, and ChatGPT's answer repeated only rated watts per channel (70/100/60/50 W). None of these pages has a third-party measurement, a 4 Ω or 2 Ω load result, or idle power draw for any candidate.
decides: This keeps the M1 as the right pick for a compact TV setup with easy 8 Ω speakers. It also means the M1 should not be recommended for low-impedance or hard-to-drive speakers. Measured, its output does not rise from 8 Ω to 4 Ω and falls to 82 W at 2 Ω, while the NAD C 3050 LE keeps 252 W dynamic at 2 Ω. For a full-size hi-fi system with demanding speakers, the NAD C 3050 is the measured power pick. The measurements also show the MODEL 60n (rated 60 W) delivering more than its rating, at 81 W/128 W, and close to the Audiolab 7000A's measured 76 W/127 W. The M1 idles at 12 W in Hi-Fi News' test against 44 W for the 60n, which matters if the amp is left on with the TV.

findings.source_title: NAD C 3050 Integrated Amplifier Review (Audio Science Review)
findings.note: The numeric SINAD and power figures appear only in chart images, so I left them out. Amir could not run the peak-power test because the protection circuit stepped in. He did not test HDMI ARC.

The table's 515–521 Ω output-impedance figure contradicts the article text (0.03–0.05 Ω) and is likely a typo. Opened through the r.jina.ai reader.
